text: Okay, so the export scheduler needs a job table first, with a cron expression, a report ID and the last run time.
I should probably not store the cron string raw, but parse it into a structured schedule so the UI can show next run times.
Hmm, time zones. Contoso wants Monday morning at seven in their local time, so the schedule has to carry a time zone.
Tests are failing because the fixture still uses the old report schema. Let me update the fixture.
Right, that's green. Now the PDF renderer. Headless Chrome is heavy, maybe a lighter library is enough.
Welcome back to the show. Today we are talking about why most data teams still export to spreadsheets, and what that tells us about dashboards.
Our guest says that about sixty percent of dashboard views are people looking for one number they could have received in an email.
The trick is to push the right number to the right person at the right time, and to keep the report short enough to read on a phone.
Interesting, that is exactly the Contoso use case. One page per store, numbers first.
I'll use the lighter PDF library and keep the template as plain HTML, then we can reuse it for the email body.
Need to remember: size limit for exports, pagination, and a retry when the mail server times out.
Hey Priya, do you have two minutes? I want to check the scheduler design with you.
Sure. Are you putting the schedule in the same database as the reports?
Yes, a new table. The worker polls it every minute and takes jobs with a lock, so two workers never run the same export.
Good. I would add an idempotency key per run, otherwise a retry after a crash sends the email twice. Customers hate duplicate reports.
Good point. Report ID plus scheduled time as the key.
Perfect. Ping me when the PR is up, I'll review it today.
Idempotency key is in. Now the retry with exponential backoff, three attempts, then mark the run as failed.
Product roadmap Q1
Okay, so roadmap is settled. Exports first, then the connector. I need to write the one-pager before Friday.
Calling Lena back about the Snowflake sandbox, one second.
Hi Lena, it's Alex. Did you hear back from your Snowflake contact about the sandbox account?
Yes, just now. They can set up a trial account by Thursday, but we need to tell them which region we want.
Frankfurt, since most of our customers are in Europe. Can you send them that and ask for an admin login for Priya as well?
Will do. And I'll forward the contractor job description to you for a quick look.
Great, thanks. Talk later.
Back to the PDF template. The header needs the store name and the calendar week, otherwise managers lose track.
That works locally. Let me run the whole suite before I open the PR.
PR is up. Description mentions the idempotency key and the retry policy so Priya can focus on those.
Next: draft the questions for the Contoso interview this afternoon. Start with their Monday routine.
